newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - DEC 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - DEC 19.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The Bank of Greece's latest report has called into question statements by National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou that the course to convergence is all but secured. The central bank stressed that, despite progress, inflation remained shaky, the balance of external payments was nearing danger levels and that competitiveness was being undermined by labour costs.
--As farmers descend on Athens in a show of strength, the Federation of Greek Industries (SEB) reveals that the daily cost of the 22-day farmers' blockade is close to 10 billion drachmas.

--London's decision to not link a Cyprus resolution to the island's accession to the European Union was reiterated by Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind to Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos yesterday.
--A survey of foreign branches of UK universities has found a number of irregularities affecting quality. There are about 100 such branches in Greece, with 25,000 students.

-- Two hundred coaches will transport protesting farmers to downtown Athens today. The government is determined to take a low profile on the rally outside Parliament and on demands for a meeting with the prime minister.

--An MRB poll shows the majority of Greeks consider the country's economy to be in a bad to very bad state and in favour of the privatisation of the telecoms organisation OTE and national carrier Olympic Airways. George Papandreou, now alternate foreign minister and formerly education, is the only minister considered to be doing a good job.
--Prime Minister Costas Simitis reiterates his determination to implement the government's economic policies without exception and to not give in to blackmail and pressure in a rare interview.
--Blocks on the country's ports continued yesterday with more instances of scuffles portside as striking dockworkers refused to let foreign flagged ships disembark passengers and lorries.
--National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou promises speedy procedures to prosecute tax evaders.

--The government will honour high-profile honest taxpayers tomorrow when it submits a list of names to Parliament. The top three are: industrialist Eleftherios Mouzakis (declared income of one billion, tax bill of 400 million); shipowner Gerasimos Agoumidos and Dominic Williams, Panathinaikos' former star player.
--Police are on the trail of the disturbed man who has been placing rocks in the high-speed lanes on the Athens-Corinth highway over the past weeks. Dozens of car accidents have been reported.
